title: Fix: Remove duplicate planning sections and align anchors (from stanlee-91z)
description:
Review of stanlee-91z found: there are two planning sections (the inline 'Travel essentials' section in app/page.tsx and the PlanningEssentials component), which duplicates content and splits the narrative. Evidence: app/page.tsx renders a practicalFacts section and also renders <PlanningEssentials />.

Acceptance criteria:
- Page contains a single planning/essentials section with one heading and one disclaimer.
- The TopNav 'Planning essentials' anchor points to the remaining section id.
- The remaining section uses the shared content model (lib/bhutan-travel-content.ts) or has a single source of truth for planning copy (no duplicated arrays).

title: Epic: Image-first Bhutan redesign with Unsplash placeholders + deployment
description: Refactor the existing Bhutan travel landing page into a photo-first experience with significantly reduced text density and external Unsplash placeholder photography. Success means every major section is led by imagery, copy is concise, accessibility remains solid, and the app is deployment-ready. Scope includes content model updates, section component refactors, Next.js image host configuration, quality gates, and deployment execution once target environment is confirmed.

title: Add Unsplash image schema to travel content
description:
## Files
- lib/bhutan-travel-content.ts (modify)

## What to do
Extend the typed content model to support image-first rendering using external Unsplash URLs. Add image src + alt fields for hero visual, each itinerary, each cultural highlight, planning essentials tiles, and testimonials where photos are displayed. Tighten copy length across exported content: keep descriptions concise and remove redundant prose so components can render less-wordy UI.

## Don't
- Don't use untyped image objects or any.
- Don't leave missing alt text for any displayed image.
- Don't include overly long multi-sentence paragraphs for card-level content.
acceptance_criteria:
- Content types compile with explicit image fields for all sections that render photos.
- Every image entry includes non-empty alt text.
- Copy length is reduced versus current version and remains contextually specific to Bhutan travel.

title: Configure Next.js external image hosting for Unsplash
description:
## Files
- next.config.mjs (modify)

## What to do
Configure Next.js image optimization to allow external Unsplash image hosts used by the redesigned page. Add precise remotePatterns entries for required Unsplash/CDN domains (not wildcard everything). Keep config minimal and compatible with current Next version.

## Don't
- Don't disable image optimization globally.
- Don't use broad '*' host allowances.
- Don't add unrelated config changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- next.config.mjs allows the exact Unsplash hostnames needed for image rendering.
- next/image can render all configured external placeholders without runtime host errors.
- No unrelated Next config regressions are introduced.

title: Refactor hero to image-dominant composition
description:
## Files
- components/travel/hero-section.tsx (modify)
- app/globals.css (modify)

## What to do
Convert the hero to a photo-led layout using next/image and Unsplash source from content data. Keep messaging concise: eyebrow, short headline, one-line support copy, two CTAs, and compact stat chips. Preserve existing lead form but reduce visual/text weight to secondary emphasis beneath the main image moment.

## Don't
- Don't remove both CTAs.
- Don't keep long paragraphs in hero body copy.
- Don't introduce layout overflow on mobile.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hero renders a large photo-first visual using next/image with alt text from content.
- Hero textual copy is visibly shorter than prior version while retaining travel intent.
- At 375px viewport, hero has no horizontal scrolling and CTAs remain visible.

title: Rebuild itinerary cards as photo-led packages
description:
## Files
- components/travel/itinerary-grid.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Refactor itinerary cards so each card starts with a dominant photo (next/image, Unsplash source), then compact metadata (duration, difficulty, start city), short bullet highlights, and one CTA. Reduce section intro copy to one concise sentence.

## Don't
- Don't remove required metadata labels.
- Don't exceed 3 highlight bullets per itinerary.
- Don't use plain div backgrounds instead of real image elements.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every itinerary card displays a visible image above text content.
- Metadata labels remain explicit and readable.
- Section copy and card text are noticeably shorter while preserving clarity.

title: Convert cultural highlights into visual tile gallery
description:
## Files
- components/travel/cultural-highlights.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Redesign cultural highlights as image-first tiles with short title/tagline and one-line supporting text. Keep responsible-travel note but compress it to a brief statement. Maintain section anchor and heading semantics.

## Don't
- Don't remove the responsible travel note entirely.
- Don't use long-form paragraph blocks per tile.
- Don't break existing section id used by in-page navigation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cultural section renders a gallery of photo-led cards/tiles.
- Each tile text is short-form (title + concise support line).
- Responsible-travel note remains present and visibly shorter than previous version.

title: Compress planning and trust sections with portrait imagery
description:
## Files
- components/travel/planning-essentials.tsx (modify)
- components/travel/trust-band.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Reduce text-heavy planning and trust sections to concise, scannable blocks. Add visual support: planning topic thumbnails/icons and traveler portrait images for testimonials (all via next/image and Unsplash placeholders). Keep trust metrics but simplify surrounding copy.

## Don't
- Don't remove disclaimer from planning section.
- Don't drop traveler name/country attribution.
- Don't exceed 5 trust metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Planning section remains present with disclaimer and significantly reduced copy density.
- Testimonials include visible portrait images with alt text plus name/country attribution.
- Trust metric row remains between 3 and 5 items.

title: Tune global visual polish for image-heavy layout
description:
## Files
- app/globals.css (modify)

## What to do
Add reusable styles for photo-real presentation: aspect-ratio helpers, subtle image overlays, compact typography utilities, and card spacing refinements that support reduced text. Ensure focus-visible and reduced-motion behavior still works with new visual effects.

## Don't
- Don't add heavy filters that obscure imagery.
- Don't remove existing focus-visible improvements.
- Don't introduce animation that ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
acceptance_criteria:
- CSS includes reusable utilities/classes used by updated image-first sections.
- New styles improve visual cohesion without harming readability.
- Existing accessibility affordances (focus-visible, reduced-motion) remain intact.

title: Run quality gates and fix regressions
description:
## Files
- app/page.tsx (modify if needed)
- components/travel/*.tsx (modify if needed)
- app/globals.css (modify if needed)

## What to do
Validate final integration of image-first redesign. Run lint, typecheck, and production build. Resolve issues related to next/image usage, external hosts, accessibility labels/alt text, anchor navigation, and responsive overflow.

## Don't
- Don't bypass errors with ts-ignore/eslint-disable unless strictly necessary and justified.
- Don't remove core sections to make checks pass.
- Don't ship with Next image host errors.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm run lint succeeds.
- npm run typecheck succeeds.
- npm run build succeeds with no external-image host runtime/config errors in the built app.

title: Deploy updated landing page to target environment
description:
## Files
- next.config.mjs (modify if deployment env requires)
- README.md (modify with deploy notes if needed)

## What to do
Deploy the redesigned app to the agreed hosting target (e.g., Vercel) using project credentials/environment. Confirm production URL serves the new image-first page and external Unsplash images load correctly. Document minimal deploy/runbook notes if anything non-obvious was required.

## Don't
- Don't hardcode secrets in repo files.
- Don't change unrelated infrastructure.
- Don't mark done without a reachable deployment URL.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deployment completes successfully to the specified target environment.
- A production URL is provided and loads the updated image-first page with Unsplash images visible.
- No secrets are committed to git.

title: Epic: Build a distinctive Bhutanese travel agent landing page
description: Create a production-grade Next.js landing page for a Bhutan-focused travel agency with a clear, memorable visual identity rooted in Bhutan-inspired color, motif, and editorial storytelling. Success means the page is fully responsive, accessible, and feels intentionally designed rather than template-like. Scope includes visual system, page sections, motion, and content architecture for a single-page marketing experience in app/page.tsx plus supporting components/styles.

title: Define Bhutan-inspired visual system and typography
description:
## Files
- app/layout.tsx (modify)
- app/globals.css (modify)

## What to do
Choose two non-generic Google fonts (one display, one body) that support Latin content and fit a Bhutanese editorial travel aesthetic. Wire them into layout variables and apply to html/body so headings and body copy can be styled distinctly. In globals.css, add a dedicated token set for this page direction: core palette, accent palette, spacing/radius decisions, and at least one decorative utility class for texture or motif framing. Keep tokens compatible with existing Tailwind v4 theme variables.

## Don't
- Don\'t use Inter, Arial, Roboto, or system UI as the primary display/body pair.
- Don\'t remove existing shadcn compatibility variables.
- Don\'t hardcode repeated hex values inside JSX once tokens exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- app/layout.tsx imports and configures exactly two intentional Google font families for display/body roles.
- app/globals.css defines reusable custom properties for brand colors and exposes at least one utility class used for decorative surface styling.
- Existing app still builds with no missing CSS variable errors from shadcn/tailwind theme mapping.

title: Finalize accessibility, SEO metadata, and quality gates
description:
## Files
- app/layout.tsx (modify)
- app/page.tsx (modify)
- package.json (modify if scripts needed)

## What to do
Add page metadata (title, description, open graph basics) aligned to Bhutan travel intent. Audit semantic structure and accessibility basics: heading order, button/link labels, input labels, alt text, and visible focus states. Run lint, typecheck, and build; fix issues introduced by the landing page work.

## Don't
- Don\'t suppress lint/type errors with ts-ignore or eslint-disable unless absolutely required and justified inline.
- Don\'t add fake structured-data claims.
- Don\'t leave any newly introduced form control unlabeled.
acceptance_criteria:
- Metadata export exists with travel-specific title and description.
- All interactive controls on page have accessible names and focus-visible styling.
- npm run lint, npm run typecheck, and npm run build succeed locally after fixes.
close_reason: c0ade2e Add Bhutan travel metadata and focus styles

title: Create structured content model for Bhutan travel page
description:
## Files
- lib/bhutan-travel-content.ts (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Create a typed content module exporting all page copy/data needed by sections: hero copy, featured itineraries, cultural highlights, practical facts, and testimonials. Include stable ids and image alt text strings where relevant so rendering can be map-driven. Refactor app/page.tsx to consume this module instead of hardcoded inline literals.

## Don't
- Don\'t fetch remote content or add CMS dependencies.
- Don\'t use any/unknown for exported data types.
- Don\'t include placeholder lorem ipsum.
acceptance_criteria:
- lib/bhutan-travel-content.ts exists and exports typed arrays/objects used by the page.
- app/page.tsx imports this module and renders at least three sections from mapped data structures.
- Typecheck passes without implicit any in the new content module.
close_reason: 637dbf1 Add structured Bhutan travel content model

title: Build immersive hero and lead-capture strip
description:
## Files
- components/travel/hero-section.tsx (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)
- app/globals.css (modify)

## What to do
Implement a hero section component with strong Bhutan travel positioning, layered visual treatment, and a prominent inquiry CTA area. Include: eyebrow label, bold headline, supporting paragraph, two CTAs (primary and secondary), and three quick stats (e.g., trips/year, local guides, avg rating). Add a compact lead-capture strip UI (name/email/travel month inputs + submit button) as a presentational form (no backend).

## Don't
- Don\'t use generic placeholder wording like "Your adventure starts here".
- Don\'t wire real form submission or API routes.
- Don\'t make CTA text vague; use travel-specific intent labels.
acceptance_criteria:
- components/travel/hero-section.tsx is rendered by app/page.tsx and includes the required copy blocks, CTA pair, and exactly three stats.
- A visible lead-capture strip with 3 inputs and 1 submit button is present in the hero area.
- Layout is responsive: no horizontal overflow at 375px viewport width.
close_reason: cc383aa Wire hero section and sunrise styles

title: Implement cultural immersion highlights section
description:
## Files
- components/travel/cultural-highlights.tsx (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Create a section that presents authentic Bhutan cultural experiences in card format (festivals, dzong architecture, monastery visits, homestay moments, etc.). Each card must include title, short description, and a small metadata line (region or best season). Include one section-level note emphasizing respectful, community-aware travel.

## Don't
- Don\'t use caricatured or exoticizing language.
- Don\'t use stock-card UI identical to default shadcn examples.
- Don\'t exceed 90 words per card description.
acceptance_criteria:
- components/travel/cultural-highlights.tsx is mounted on the page with at least 4 cultural cards.
- Each card shows title, description, and one metadata line.
- Section includes a visible responsible-travel note and contains no demeaning or stereotyped phrasing.

title: Build featured itineraries section with duration and difficulty
description:
## Files
- components/travel/itinerary-grid.tsx (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Add a featured itineraries section rendering trip packages as visually distinct panels. Each itinerary must display: name, duration, difficulty level, starting city, and 3 bullet highlights. Include a clear CTA button per itinerary (e.g., request custom quote). Ensure cards can stack gracefully on mobile.

## Don't
- Don\'t use tables.
- Don\'t leave package metadata unlabeled.
- Don\'t render fewer than 3 itinerary options.
acceptance_criteria:
- components/travel/itinerary-grid.tsx appears on app/page.tsx and renders at least 3 itinerary cards.
- Every itinerary card includes the required metadata fields and exactly one CTA button.
- On mobile width (<= 640px), cards render in a single column without clipped text.

title: Add travel planning essentials section
description:
## Files
- components/travel/planning-essentials.tsx (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Implement a practical information section covering visa/permit guidance, best travel windows, altitude prep, and sustainability expectations. Present as concise checklist or split panels with clear headings and icon support where useful. Include a short disclaimer that details are guidance and final requirements should be confirmed before booking.

## Don't
- Don\'t provide legal guarantees or absolute claims.
- Don\'t include external links unless already present elsewhere in project.
- Don\'t bury this section below footer content.
acceptance_criteria:
- components/travel/planning-essentials.tsx is rendered on page with at least 4 planning topics.
- A disclaimer sentence about verifying official requirements is visible in this section.
- Section heading and subheadings use semantic heading tags in descending order.

title: Create social proof and trust band
description:
## Files

- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Build a section combining traveler testimonials and trust signals (years operating, local partnerships, support availability). Render at least 2 testimonial quotes with names + origin country and a separate compact trust metrics row. Keep copy specific and grounded.

- Don\'t use anonymous quote attribution like "Happy Traveler".

acceptance_criteria:

title: Implement sticky navigation and conversion footer
description:
## Files
- components/travel/top-nav.tsx (create)
- components/travel/page-footer.tsx (create)
- app/page.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Add a sticky top navigation with agency namemark, section anchors, and primary contact CTA. Add a footer with contact channels, office location text, and final conversion CTA. Ensure anchor links scroll to corresponding sections and maintain usable contrast in both light and dark mode.

## Don't
- Don\'t create separate routes; keep this a single-page section-anchor experience.
- Don\'t use placeholder contact values like 123-456-7890.
- Don\'t hide key CTA behind hover-only interactions.
acceptance_criteria:
- top-nav and page-footer components are both rendered in app/page.tsx.
- Navigation includes working in-page anchor links that target existing section ids.
- Footer includes at least one phone/email contact method and one explicit booking CTA button.
close_reason: b3291b5 Add sticky nav and conversion footer

title: Add high-impact motion with reduced-motion fallback
description:
## Files
- app/globals.css (modify)
- app/page.tsx (modify)
- components/travel/*.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Introduce one cohesive entrance animation system (staggered reveal across hero and first two sections) and meaningful hover/focus transitions for primary interactive elements. Implement prefers-reduced-motion handling that disables non-essential movement while preserving usability. Use CSS-first animation strategy.

## Don't
- Don\'t add animation libraries.
- Don\'t animate layout properties that cause jank on scroll.
- Don\'t keep animations active when reduced-motion is requested.
acceptance_criteria:
- Page includes visible staged entrance motion on initial load for multiple section elements.
- Hover/focus transitions exist for primary buttons/links and are keyboard-accessible.
- A prefers-reduced-motion media query is present and meaningfully reduces/removes non-essential animations.
close_reason: 50dd79e Add staggered motion and reduced-motion fallbacks

title: Fix: Hero motif card hides text from screen readers (from stanlee-91z)
description:
Review of stanlee-91z found: the hero motif card uses role=img on a container with real text, so screen readers may ignore the content. Evidence: components/travel/hero-section.tsx figure has role="img" and aria-label while containing headings and copy.

Acceptance criteria:
- The hero motif card content remains visually identical but is read by screen readers.
- No element that contains readable text uses role=img.
- If an image-like label is still needed, provide accessible text without hiding the internal content.
close_reason: c67b788 Make hero motif card readable
